chunk-001:c003.proposition: Analogical predication attributes knowledge and power to God's single essence without identifying the distinct creaturely properties of knowledge and power.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Divine simplicity requires real identity between God and everything intrinsic to God while allowing grounded conceptual distinctions among divine attributes and extrinsic contingent predications.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Divine aseity supports simplicity because intrinsic parts distinct from God would make God's being or intrinsic properties depend upon something that is not God.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: A purely actual first being cannot contain the potentiality involved in the traditional kinds of metaphysical composition and therefore lacks such composition.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: A Latin Trinitarian model preserves simplicity by identifying each person and procession with the divine nature while distinguishing the persons through opposed relations.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: The Son is identical with his begottenness, whose relational directedness distinguishes him from the Father without adding a positive ontological item to the divine essence.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Changing divine knowledge involves changing extrinsic truths rather than a change in God's intrinsic ontological features, so contingent omniscience need not introduce potency in God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Divine knowledge consists intrinsically in an unchanging intellect and causal efficacy, while differences between temporally indexed objects of knowledge are wholly extrinsic.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: A perfectly good and self-sufficient God can refrain from creating because creation adds no goodness to God and is a gratuitous act ordered to creatures and divine glory.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-05.proposition: Changing God-world relations do not introduce intrinsic change or temporality in God because those relations inhere in creatures rather than in God.
